slot.brief: Definite/indefinite integral needing integration by parts (log x or inverse trig times x) or a partial-fraction split

working:
$u=\tan^{-1}x$, $dv=x\,dx$.
$\displaystyle \int_0^1 x\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1}x\right]_0^1-\frac12\int_0^1\frac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx$
$=\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac12[x-\tan^{-1}x]_0^1=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12$.

Independent check: Integration by parts gives \(\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac12\int_0^1\frac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx=\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac12(1-\frac{\pi}{4})=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12\).
solution:
Using integration by parts with $u=\tan^{-1}x$ and $dv=x\,dx$,
$$\int_0^1 x\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1}x\right]_0^1-\frac12\int_0^1\frac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx$$
$=\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac12\left(1-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac12$.

B: Sign error in the remaining integral after integration by parts.
